title: Mon 2 Nov: Nifty edges up on IT as Nasdaq slides
description:
Hot topic: India's Nifty closed Friday up 0.5% on an IT rally, then Wall Street's tech rout hit, on the eve of the US midterms. Then: Hormuz mines, Bank of Baroda, Sun Pharma, the rupee, Indian IT, Dixon, ITC, US yields and IndiGo.

1. Nifty rises 0.5% to 23,053 on an IT rally as Amazon and Intel hit Wall Street before the US midterms (5paisa; Tech Insider; Bloomberg via Swissinfo; Tapetide)
2. Iran says two more tankers hit mines in Hormuz as fears grow of US strikes around the midterms (Al Jazeera; Investing.com; Bloomberg via Swissinfo)
3. Bank of Baroda's Q2 profit jumps 36% to 6,532 crore rupees, beating estimates, as gross NPAs fall to 1.78% (Whalesbook; Indian Masterminds)
4. Sun Pharma's Q2 profit falls 36% on a 1,269 crore rupee one-time loss as US sales drop 8% (Business Standard; TenNews)
5. Rupee jumps 33 paise to 94.93 on a weaker dollar and RBI intervention (PTI via Metrovaartha; Tapetide)
6. Indian IT jumps 2.3% on Cognizant's results while the Nasdaq sinks on Amazon and Intel (5paisa; Tech Insider)
7. Dixon's Q2 profit falls 45% to 411 crore rupees even as revenue jumps 47% (Free Press Journal)
8. ITC reports Q2 on Monday with the stock near its 52-week low (NiftyTrader)
9. Treasury yields slip toward 4.94% as Big Tech's sell-off drives a flight to safety (Bloomberg via Swissinfo; Tech Insider)
10. IndiGo jumps 4.3% after a narrower Q2 loss as Brent stays above 110 dollars (5paisa; Bloomberg via Swissinfo)

From the Ripple news desk. Voices are AI-generated with open-source Kokoro voices. This is news, not investment advice; the hosts are not SEBI-registered advisers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Good morning, this is Ripple Daily. I'm P.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: And I'm S. Ten stories, under ten minutes.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Today's big one: India rallied on Friday, then Wall Street had a rout. Who wins Monday?

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: S, start with Friday. What happened?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The Nifty closed at 23,053, up 0.51%. The Sensex rose 0.42% to 74,459. But Nifty Bank actually slipped 0.41%.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Who moved?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Trent led, up 5.4% on its results. IndiGo rose 4.3%, and Infosys 3.4% on an IT rally.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And then America sold off.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Sharply. After India closed, the S&P 500 fell 1.82% and the Nasdaq 2.86%, as Intel and Amazon hit chip stocks.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Okay, but why should India care about Intel?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Now, why it matters. India has to absorb a near 3% Nasdaq fall, plus Gulf headlines, on the eve of Tuesday's US midterms.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: And foreign money is fickle. FIIs bought a net 3,599 crore rupees on Friday, but sold 45,162 crore over October.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Any early signals this morning?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Mixed. S&P 500 futures were up 0.3% early Monday, but Japan's Topix was down 0.6%.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: So what's the trigger to watch?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Whether domestic buying and results keep the index firm. If the US sell-off carries into Asia and FIIs turn sellers again, the Nifty ends lower.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And the stocks?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Stocks in focus: HDFC Bank, the heaviest Nifty weight, ICICI Bank, Infosys and Trent. Sentiment: mixed.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Rapid fire. Story two: Iran says more tankers hit mines in Hormuz, as strike fears grow.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says talks on a two-day plan to reopen the strait are under way, through Qatari mediators.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: But only if Washington offers sanctions relief, released funds and restored oil waivers. And the IRGC says two more crude tankers hit mines.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What did oil do?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Brent fell 1.5% to about 111.71 dollars in early Asian trade. OPEC+ kept its December output targets unchanged.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: Brent above 110 dollars is the biggest swing factor for India's fuel bill and the rupee. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: ONGC, BPCL, IOC, Great Eastern Shipping.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story three: Bank of Baroda beats, and bad loans shrink.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Q2 profit rose 35.8% to 6,531 crore rupees, against a preview of about 5,290 crore. Gross NPAs fell to 1.78%.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Any catch?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Net interest income grew only 9%, and the quarter included a 1,372 crore gain on selling NSE shares. Today is the first session to react.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: a clean asset-quality print sets the tone for SBI and other state banks this week. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: Bank of Baroda, SBI, PNB, Canara Bank.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story four: Sun Pharma's profit drops 36%. How bad is it?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Much of it is a 1,269 crore rupee one-time loss. But US formulation sales fell 8.2% to 455 million dollars, and margin slipped to 29.3%.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Anything good in there?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: India sales rose 17%, and profit before one-offs rose 6.3%. The stock closed 0.95% higher on Friday, at 1,777.70 rupees.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: a US generics slowdown at India's largest drugmaker weighs on pharma sentiment. Sentiment: negative. Stocks in focus: Sun Pharma, Cipla, Divi's Labs.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story five: the rupee has a good day.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The rupee rose 33 paise to 94.93 per dollar on Friday, from 95.26, helped by a weaker dollar and RBI intervention.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Will it last?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Brent's slide this morning helps. But Friday's Nasdaq fall argues for risk-off. The level to watch is 95.07.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: a firmer rupee eases imported inflation, though it trims the edge for IT exporters. Sentiment: positive.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story six: Indian IT rallied, then the Nasdaq fell. Who blinks?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Nifty IT rose 2.3% on Friday after Cognizant's results, and Infosys rose 3.4% to 1,185 rupees.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Then in New York, the SOXX chip ETF fell 9.1%, as Intel and Amazon deepened worries about AI spending.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Anything on the calendar?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Infosys's 26 rupee interim dividend has its record date tomorrow, Tuesday 3 November.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: IT led India's October rally, so a US tech rout tests whether the sector holds its gains. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: Infosys, TCS, HCLTech, Wipro.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story seven: Dixon sells a lot more, but earns a lot less.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Revenue rose 47% to 21,794 crore rupees. Profit fell 45% to 411 crore, as other income collapsed.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Anything else worrying?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Auditors flagged 1,110 crore of PLI receivables. And the stock had already fallen 4.2% to 11,000 rupees on Friday, before the results.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: India's largest contract electronics maker shows margins squeezed even as phone volumes grow. Sentiment: negative. Stocks in focus: Dixon, PG Electroplast, Havells.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story eight: ITC reports today, with the stock near its 52-week low.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: YES Securities expects profit of about 3,926 crore rupees, down about 23%, with cigarette volumes down about 6% after tax increases.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And where's the stock?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: It closed Friday at 265.60 rupees, near its 52-week low of 252.80, and it's down about 28% this year.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: ITC is the biggest test of how far higher cigarette taxes are hitting volumes. Sentiment: negative. Stocks in focus: ITC, Hindustan Unilever, VST Industries.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story nine: US bond yields, and why a Fed hike is back on the table.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The 10-year Treasury yield was about 4.94% this morning, after the Big Tech sell-off pushed money into bonds.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Futures price a 75 to 85% chance of a December Fed hike. October payrolls on Friday are expected at 55,000.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: US yields near 5% set the cost of capital for emerging markets, and FII appetite for India. Sentiment: negative.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Last one. Story ten: IndiGo flies higher, despite oil.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: IndiGo rose 4.3% to 4,877.60 rupees on Friday, after a narrower-than-expected Q2 loss and 34% higher fares.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: But fuel is still expensive, right?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Very. Fuel cost per seat rose 69%, and jet fuel is IndiGo's largest cost.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: the stock trades on every Gulf headline, and Brent is still above 110 dollars. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: IndiGo.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What to watch today: does the Nifty shrug off Wall Street, what does ITC report, and does Brent stay below 112 dollars?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: That's Ripple Daily. Full stories and sources are in the show notes. This is news, not investment advice. We're not SEBI-registered advisers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: See you tomorrow morning.
